stance_basis: letter endorses project and noise mitigation but suggests alternatives to earthen berms and requests review of lighting solutions
summary: The City Administration, represented by City Manager William J. Leidinger, submitted a formal comment letter expressing general support for the Randolph Urban Renewal Project and agreement with its environmental conclusions, while raising specific concerns about the proposed earthen berms as noise barriers and the light spill issue. The Administration suggested that a wall on the expressway side of Grayland Avenue might be a preferable alternative to berms, and committed to reviewing lighting alternatives with the Richmond Metropolitan Authority. The letter also noted several minor factual errors in the draft statement.
complaint_summary: The City Administration generally endorses the project and its environmental conclusions but suggests that a wall rather than earthen berms may be a preferable acoustical barrier along Grayland Avenue, requests review of light spill alternatives with the Richmond Metropolitan Authority, and notes several minor errors in the draft statement.

statement.text:
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on the Draft Environmental Statement for the Randolph Urban Renewal Area (VA-R-58) forwarded with your letter of March 2, 1973.
This statement appears to be very complete and quite helpful to us in assessing the validity of the project, particularly in relation to the planned Downtown Expressway. We certainly agree with the conclusion reached in the report that the various environmental impacts resulting from the project will be of short-term nature and that the long-term benefits to the community will greatly exceed the adverse effects noted.
The proposals for providing proper acoustical shielding between the Downtown Expressway and nearby areas of the Randolph neighborhood appear appropriate. The earthen berms and remedial treatment of structures can be incorporated within the scope of the Randolph Urban Renewal Project without difficulty.
With respect to the use of earthen berms, we are inclined to believe that a wall located on the expressway side of Grayland Avenue could be constructed at a lower height than the berms and achieve equivalent acoustical benefits. In addition, the long-term
1

Mr. Theodore R. Robb Page 2 March 28, 1973
cost of maintaining a landscaped berm and the extensive land required for it would appear to be a disadvantage inherent in the berm approach. We recognize that a berm located as shown in the Statement has the value of shielding the neighborhood from the noise of traffic on Grayland Avenue; however, there may be some obstruction of vision at intersections which could be avoided by the use of a wall on the north side of Grayland Avenue. Obviously, comparative costs and the feasibility of adapting a wall structure to the location and grade of the slopes required for the Downtown Expressway must be examined before a valid comparison can be made. We endorse in principal the concept of shielding the Randolph neighborhood from the noise of traffic on the Expressway and simply take this opportunity to suggest that the final Statement present the landscaped berm as one means of accomplishing that objective without precluding development of more desirable alternatives.
The only other adverse impact which the Statement suggests might be mitigated is the matter of light spill on adjacent areas from the Downtown Expressway. The Statement acknowledges the various views of residents, both pro and con, which might be anticipated. Furthermore, the cost and availability of specialized lighting fixtures and the effects on traffic safety resulting from reduction in the level of illumination on the Expressway are unknown at this time. The City Administration will review with the Richmond Metropolitan Authority alternatives which appear feasible and desirable in view of the various considerations involved. It is my hope that a solution will be possible which minimizes adverse environmental effects without limiting traffic safety.
Several minor errors are noted in the report as follows:
1. Descriptions of Areas (1) and (2) are transposed on pages 9 and 10.
2. The bridge indicated for Lombardy Street in the illustration on page 17 is not correct and should be deleted.
3. The first line of A (3) contains the word "with" which should be changed to "will" in order to convey the proper meaning.

Mr. Theodore R. Robb Page 3 March 28, 1973
I am pleased to have this opportunity to comment on the Environmental Statement for the Randolph Urban Renewal Project. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions. We are committed to proceeding with implementation of the renewal plan and hope that we will be able to move ahead promptly.
Sincerely,
William J. Leidinge
City Manager
